reader.requirement: At --std 85 a successful OPEN makes the relative file's record area available, and for an EXTERNAL file connector every program of the run unit that describes the file (contained or separately written, under any record description) shares the one record area, so a MOVE, WRITE or READ in one program is seen in the others.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 also checks that the describing programs' file descriptions agree (CheckFileDescriptions); picks the edition's citation

reader.edition-search: grep of the external-file binding (BinderDriver ::EXT:: band, DataBinder.IsInExternalRecord, FileRegistry.RegisterRelative) for EditionContext|DialectLevel; only ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check consults it, for the consistency screen, not for the shared record area.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the shared record area; the 85 arm adds a description-consistency screen
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf24_02 covers a contained program with the same record description; separately written programs, a different record description of the shared area, and an OPEN made in a called program are not exercised

probes.printed: SUB1 OPEN 00 / MAIN AFTER SUB OPEN 00 [SUB1ASUB1B] / MAIN WRITE 1 00 / SUB2 SEES MAIN-AREA1 / SUB2 WRITE 2 00 / MAIN SEES SUB2-AREA / R1=SUB1ASUB1B / R2=SUB2-REC-2 / SUB2 SEES SUB2-REC-2
probes.expected: one record area: the group view (QX-A/QX-B) and the elementary view of separate programs alias it; the OPEN in GR2SUB1 serves WRITEs in GR2MAIN and GR2SUB2; a READ in main is seen by the sub

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: An EXTERNAL FD's FileModel is renamed into the ::EXT:: band so every describing program reaches one runtime connector (RegisterRelative returns early for an existing one) and the FD's records are external records sharing storage. Probed with three separately written programs in one source file.

refuter.evidence: Probe runs/r2_extlocal-001 has an EXTERNAL relative FD in the main program with two record descriptions (X(10) and a group of 3+7), a contained program describing it EXTERNAL with another group shape, and a separately written program with a NON-external FD of the same file-name on another file. It printed MAIN OPEN 00 / LOCAL OPEN 00 / LOCAL WRITE 00 [LOCALAREA1] / MAIN AFTER LOCAL [MAINAREA01] / NEST SEES [MAINAREA01] / MAIN AFTER NEST [NESTAREA01] G1=NES / R1=NESTAREA01 00. So there is one record area for the external connector, the non-external namesake does not alias it, and a record written through the shared area reads back. Read ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check (the 85 arm CheckFileDescriptions is a consistency screen and does not refuse this legal program). cite.py: OK  §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2
